hook: SCP-330 is a steel bowl of wrapped candy with a handwritten note asking you to take no more than two. That is the whole premise, and it is enough. It is a short Halloween-flavored file, and the punishment for greed is described bluntly, so expect severed hands.
whyItMatters:
This is a pure one-rule anomaly: the condition fits on a sticky note, it is impossible not to read, and breaking it costs you both hands. Rules that simple invite the reader to start hunting for loopholes, and the article anticipates that by testing the edges for you.

The tone also matters. The file is dry and procedural about something that is essentially a children's warning, which is where most of its dark humor comes from.
thingsToNotice:
Every escape route is closed in a sentence or two: the note cannot be removed or covered, it can be read even from the far side, and a D-class working a remote manipulator still loses their own hands. The discovery story escalates the stakes, since the police officers who seized the bowl as evidence all died after one of them emptied it, with the cause expunged.

The single experiment is the clever part, because it asks what happens to someone who has no hands to lose. A double amputee takes three pieces, then feels burning stumps and phantom wrists until he tears off his prostheses, breaks down when made to wear a fresh pair, and only manages it once twenty-four hours have passed. He is kept alive for a cold practical reason: D-class amputees already used to prosthetics are hard to find.
